author: Test Forecaster A
weather_discussion:
Models do not predict any snowfall through Thursday night. After a warm start to the work week, a dry cold front should move through the area Tuesday. Long-range models predict unsettled spring weather by the weekend. Take 3-5 day forecasts with a big grain of salt in the spring. Some details:

Monday: Temperature inversions kept middle and upper elevation locations above freezing Sunday night. Expect mostly clear skies, temperatures in the 40s and possibly lower 50s F, and mostly light S-W winds.

Tuesday: Temperature inversions should keep the mountains in the 30s and lower 40s F Monday night. A cold front will produce partly to mostly cloudy skies, and SW-W winds will build to moderate to strong speeds. Temperatures should remain static or warm slightly to the upper 30s and lower 40s F. 

Wednesday:  Tuesday night should bring clearing skies, much colder temperatures in the teens to upper 20s F, and light to moderate NW-W winds. Wednesday, expect clear to partly cloudy skies, temperatures in the 30s and lower 40s F, and breezy, light to moderate NW-W winds.  

Thursday: Models predict below freezing temperatures in most locations on Wednesday night, followed by clear to partly cloudy skies, warmer temps in the 40s F, and light to moderate W winds on Thursday.  

Friday-Sun: Longer-range models bring warm, showery weather to the area, with rain-snow lines beginning near 9000'.
